questions.question: When a large force acts on a body for a short time, then the force is called?
questions.solution:
__
 
• When a large force acts on a body for a short time, then the force is called **impulsive force.__**
 
• Impulse = force x time = change in momentum
 
• Impulse is a vector quantity.
 
• SI Unit of Impulse is Newton second (Ns).

__**Explanation:**__

Impulse

 
• When a large force works on a body for a very small time interval, it is called impulsive force.
 
• An impulsive force does not remain constant, but changes first from zero to maximum and then from maximum to zero. In such a case, we measure the total effect of force.
 
• The impulse caused by a force during a specific time interval is equal to the body's change of momentum during that time interval.
 
• Impulse, effectively, is a measure of change in momentum.
 
• The impulse of a force is a measure of the total effect of force.
 
• Impulse is a vector quantity and its direction is the same as that of force.
 
• SI unit of impulse is Newton-second or kg-m-s-1 and CGS unit is g.m/s

questions.question:
Consider the following pairs:

 
 

 **Case**
 **Popular for**
 
 

 1. Kesavanandha Bharati case
 Basic Structure doctrine
 
 

 2. Kihoto Hollohan case
 Defection
 
 

 3. M. Nagraj case
 Curative petition
 
 

 4. Rupa Ashok Hurra case
 Reservations in promotions
 
 

Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ​**__1 and 2 only__.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• In the **Kesavananda Bharati case (1973)**, the Supreme Court laid down a new doctrine of the ‘**basic structure’** (or ‘basic features’) of the Constitution. *Hence, pair 1 is correct.*

 
 
• It ruled that the constituent power of Parliament under Article 368 does not enable it to alter the ‘basic structure’ of the Constitution.
 
• The present position is that the Parliament under Article 368 can amend any part of the Constitution including the Fundamental Rights but without affecting the ‘basic structure’ of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• In the **Kihoto Hollohan vs Zachillhu And Others (1992) case**, a constitutional challenge to the **Tenth Schedule (Defection law) **was settled by the apex court.
 
 
• The court upheld the sweeping discretion available to the Speaker in deciding cases of disqualification of MLAs.
 
• Hence the case is popularly referred to as the **Defection case. ***Hence, pair 2 is correct.*
 
 
 
• In the **M. Nagaraj v. Union of India (2006) case**, the Court validated Parliament's decision to extend reservations for SC/STs to include promotions **(reservation in promotion). ***Hence, pair 3 is incorrect.*
 
 
• The Supreme court held that in order to provide reservations in promotions for SCs/STs, the State has to collect quantifiable data showing: backwardness of the class and inadequacy of representation of that class in public employment in addition to compliance of Article 335.
 
 
• **Article 335** recognises that special measures need to be adopted for considering the claims of SCs and STs in order to bring them to a level-playing field.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Rupa Ashok Hurra case: **The Supreme court of India evolved the concept of the **curative petition** in the landmark case of Rupa Ashok Hurra vs. Ashok Hurra and Anr. (**2002**). ***Hence, pair 4 is incorrect.***
 
 
• In this case, the apex court health with the question, whether an aggrieved person is entitled to any relief against the final order/judgment of the Supreme court after the dismissal of review petition.

questions.question: Which Mauryan pillar inscription is located in the easternmost part of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sarnath**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

__ 
 
• The **Mauryan pillar** located at **Sarnath** is one of the most renowned monuments of the Mauryan dynasty. It is situated near Varanasi in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh. 
 
• The Sarnath pillar is particularly famous as it bears the **Lion Capital of Ashoka**, which was later adopted as the National Emblem of India. 
 
• This pillar was erected by **Emperor Ashoka** in the 3rd century BCE, commemorating the site where Buddha delivered his first sermon, known as the **Dharmachakra Pravartana (Turning of the Wheel of Dharma)**. 
 
• The inscription on the Sarnath pillar contains edicts promoting **Buddhist values**, such as non-violence, compassion, and moral conduct. 
 
• The pillar’s **easternmost location** among Mauryan pillars signifies Ashoka's dedication to spreading his policies and Buddhist teachings across a vast region. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 

__ 
 
• **Mauryan Pillars:** 
 
• The Mauryan pillars were built during the reign of Emperor Ashoka (268-232 BCE) as a part of his efforts to disseminate his edicts and Buddhist philosophy. 
 
• These pillars are made of **polished sandstone** and are remarkable for their intricate carvings and inscriptions. 
 
• Most of these pillars have inscriptions in the **Brahmi script** and are written in the **Prakrit language**. 
 
 

 
• **Sarnath Lion Capital:** 
 
• The Lion Capital at Sarnath consists of four lions standing back-to-back, symbolizing **power, courage, and confidence**. 
 
• It is mounted on a circular abacus, adorned with carvings of animals like elephants, horses, bulls, and lions, representing the four cardinal directions. 
 
• The abacus also features the **Dharmachakra (Wheel of Dharma)**, signifying the universal spread of Buddhist teachings. 
 
 

 
• **Other Mauryan Pillars:** 
 
• **Sanchi:** Located in Madhya Pradesh, Sanchi is famous for its stupas and gateways rather than pillars. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. 
 
• **Topra:** Originally located in Haryana, the Topra pillar is another Ashokan pillar later moved to Feroz Shah Kotla in Delhi by Sultan Feroz Shah Tughlaq. 
 
• **Meerut:** The Ashokan pillar at Meerut, Uttar Pradesh, is another example of the Mauryan architecture, showcasing Ashoka's inscriptions. 
 
 

 
• **Emperor Ashoka:** 
 
• He was a significant ruler of the Mauryan Empire, known for his conversion to Buddhism after the **Kalinga War**. 
 
• Ashoka’s reign is marked by the spread of Buddhist teachings across the Indian subcontinent and beyond to regions like Sri Lanka, Central Asia, and Southeast Asia. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 

 
 
• **Architectural Features of Mauryan Pillars:** 
 
• The pillars are typically monolithic, with a tapering shaft topped by a capital (often with animal sculptures). 
 
• They are made of **Chunar sandstone**, known for its fine finish and polish. 
 
• The inscriptions reflect Ashoka’s **Dhamma policy**, emphasizing non-violence, tolerance, and welfare for all. 
 
 

 
• **Significance of the Pillars:** 
 
• They served as a medium to communicate the policies of Ashoka and promote Buddhist principles. 
 
• The pillars highlight the **advanced craftsmanship** and engineering skills of the Mauryan period. 
 
 

 
• **Adoption of the Lion Capital as National Emblem:** 
 
• The Lion Capital of Ashoka was adopted as the National Emblem of India on **26 January 1950**. 
 
• It symbolizes the **sovereignty of India** and the government’s commitment to upholding truth and justice.

questions.solution:

__
 
• **Surkotada** is a significant **Harappan site located in Gujarat**, India.
 
• This site was discovered in **1964** by **J.P. Joshi** of the Archaeological Survey of India.
 
• Surkotada is known for its unique fortification, and it provides evidence of the Harappan civilization's expansion into the Gujarat region.
 
• The site is notable for the discovery of horse remains, which are rarely found in other Harappan sites.
 
• Surkotada had a small fortified settlement with mud-brick structures, indicating urban planning and architectural proficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Sokhta Koh:**

 
 
• Sokhta Koh is located in **Baluchistan, Pakistan**, near the Makran coast.
 
• It is believed to have served as a trading post for Harappans, facilitating maritime trade.
 
• The site is known for its connection to the Harappan civilization's coastal trade network.
 
 
 
• **Shortugai:**
 
 
• Shortugai is located in **Afghanistan**, near the Amu Darya river.
 
• This site was a significant trading center for Harappans, particularly for importing lapis lazuli.
 
• It provides evidence of Harappan influence beyond the Indian subcontinent.
 
 
 
• **Sutkagendor:**
 
 
• Sutkagendor is situated in the **Baluchistan province of Pakistan**, near the Iranian border.
 
• The site is believed to have functioned as a coastal trade post for the Harappan civilization.
 
• Sutkagendor connects the Harappan civilization to its maritime trade networks.
 
 
 
• **Harappan Civilization:**
 
 
• The Harappan civilization, also known as the **Indus Valley Civilization**, thrived between **2600 BCE to 1900 BCE**.
 
• It was characterized by urban planning, advanced architecture, and trade networks.
 
• Major sites include **Harappa, Mohenjo-Daro, Lothal, Kalibangan, and Dholavira**.
 
• It is one of the world's earliest urban civilizations, alongside Mesopotamia and Egypt.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Surkotada's Importance:**

 
 
• Surkotada provides evidence of Harappan civilization's **geographical spread** into Gujarat.
 
• The discovery of **horse remains** at Surkotada is significant, as horses are rarely found at Harappan sites.
 
• The site demonstrates the Harappan civilization's adaptability in different geographical and ecological conditions.
 
 
 
• **Harappan Sites in Gujarat:**
 
 
• Prominent Harappan sites in Gujarat include **Lothal, Dholavira, Rangpur, and Surkotada**.
 
• These sites highlight the influence of the Harappan civilization in western India.
 
• They are known for their unique features like dockyards (Lothal), water reservoirs (Dholavira), and fortified settlements (Surkotada).

questions.question: Two cards are drawn successively without replacement from a well-shuffled pack of 52 cards. The probability of drawing two aces is

Probability of the first card being an ace = 4/52 = 1/13.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The ratio of corresponding sides of similar triangles is exactly equal to the square root of the ratio of their areas.

⇒ Ratio of corresponding sides = √121 : √225

⇒ Ratio of corresponding sides = 11 : 15

**∴ The correct answer is 11 : 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of the areas of two similar triangles = 121 : 225

**Formula Used:**

For any two similar triangles, the ratio of their areas is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides: Area₁ / Area₂ = (Side₁ / Side₂)²

 

 Area = 121
 Side 1
 
 

 Area = 225
 Side 2

**Calculations:**

Let the areas of the two similar triangles be A₁ and A₂, and their corresponding sides be S₁ and S₂ respectively.

⇒ A₁ / A₂ = 121 / 225

⇒ (S₁ / S₂)² = 121 / 225

Taking the square root on both sides,

⇒ S₁ / S₂ = √(121 / 225)

⇒ S₁ / S₂ = 11 / 15

⇒ S₁ : S₂ = 11 : 15

**∴ The correct answer is 11 : 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio of Perimeters

The ratio of the perimeters of two similar triangles is directly equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Ratio of Medians and Altitudes

The ratio of the corresponding medians, corresponding altitudes, and corresponding angle bisectors of two similar triangles is exactly equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Volumes of Similar Solid Figures

If two solid geometric figures are similar, the ratio of their volumes is equal to the cube of the ratio of their corresponding linear dimensions (V₁ / V₂ = (S₁ / S₂)³).

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Distance covered in 1 revolution = 2 × (22/7) × 2.1 = 13.2 m

Speed in m/min = 75 × 13.2 = 990 m/min

Speed in kmph = (990 × 60) ÷ 1000 = 59.4 kmph

**∴ The correct answer is 59.4 kmph.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the wheel (r) = 2.1 m

Number of revolutions (n) = 75 per minute

**Formula Used:**

Distance covered in 1 revolution = Circumference = 2 × π × r

Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9315604e5810d980322bf39a514071e8f34ad3a2eafa341d15a60bce26004d70.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Circumference = 2 × (22/7) × 2.1

⇒ Circumference = 2 × 22 × 0.3 = 13.2 m

⇒ Distance covered in 1 minute = 75 × 13.2 = 990 m

⇒ Distance covered in 60 minutes (1 hour) = 990 × 60 = 59400 m

⇒ Speed in kmph = 59400 ÷ 1000 = 59.4 kmph

**∴ The correct answer is 59.4 kmph.**

Revolutions and Distance

Speed Conversion

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

John said to me, "I had forgotten my passport."

options.text: John told me that I had forgotten his passport.
John told me that I had forgotten my possport.
John told me that he had forgotten his passport.
John told me that he has forgotten his passport.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** John said to me, "I had forgotten my passport."
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Reporting Verb:** "said to" changes to **"told"** when followed by an object (me).
 
• **Pronoun Change:** The first-person pronoun **"I"** changes to **"he"** to refer back to the subject (John). The possessive **"my"** changes to **"his"**.
 
• **Tense Change:** The original sentence is in the **Past Perfect** tense ("had forgotten").
 
 
• According to the rules of indirect speech, the **Past Perfect remains unchanged** because there is no further "back" in time to move.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"John told me that he had forgotten his passport."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "John told me that I had forgotten his passport."

 
 
• Incorrect pronoun: "I" suggests the listener forgot the passport, which changes the original meaning.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "John told me that I had forgotten my passport."
 
 
• Incorrect pronoun and spelling: Uses "I" instead of "he" and contains a typo ("possport").
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "John told me that he has forgotten his passport."
 
 
• Incorrect tense: "Has forgotten" is Present Perfect. We cannot move from Past Perfect "forward" to Present Perfect in indirect speech.

questions.question: Choose the correct option to complete the sentence. Hardly ______ the lecture begun when the electricity went out.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 1' i.e. had .

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of an** inverted sentence structure**, often used with words like "hardly," "scarcely," or "no sooner."
 
• In such sentences, the helping verb comes before the subject, and the structure follows the rule: **Hardly + had + subject + past participle + when + event.**
 
• “Had” is used in combination with the past participle to indicate that one action was completed before another began.

Correct sentence: *Hardly **had** the lecture begun when the electricity went out.*

• **Scarcely/No sooner:** These words also follow similar inverted sentence structures.

 
 
• **Example with scarcely:** Scarcely had she arrived when the meeting started.
 
• **Example with no sooner:** No sooner had he finished his meal than he left the house.
 
 
 
• Inverted sentence structures are used to emphasize the sequence of events and add a formal tone to the sentence.

questions.question: Identify the sentence that correctly follows the sequence of tenses in reported speech.

options.text: He said that he will attend the meeting.
He said that he would attend the meeting.
He said that he attends the meeting.
He said that he attending the meeting.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 2' i.e. He said that he would attend the meeting .

__
 
• The sentence is in **reported speech**, which requires the sequence of tenses to be maintained.
 
• In reported speech, when the reporting verb (e.g., "He said") is in the past tense, the verb in the reported clause must also be adjusted accordingly.
 
• Option 2, **"He said that he would attend the meeting," **correctly follows the rule. Here, "would" is the past tense of "will," maintaining the sequence of tenses.
 
• Let us analyze other options:
 
 
• Option 1: "He said that he will attend the meeting" is incorrect because "will" does not match the past tense of the reporting verb.
 
• Option 3: "He said that he attends the meeting" is incorrect because the verb "attends" is in the present simple, which does not align with the past reporting verb.
 
• Option 4: "He said that he attending the meeting" is grammatically incorrect due to improper verb form usage.
 
 

Correct sentence: *He said that he would attend the meeting*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In reported speech:
 
 
• **Direct Speech:** He said, "I will attend the meeting."
 
• **Reported Speech:** He said that he would attend the meeting.
 
 
 
• **Key Rule:** "Will" changes to "would" in reported speech when the reporting verb is in the past tense.
 
• This adjustment ensures proper sequence of tenses, which is essential for grammatical accuracy in English.
